title: Attention Kernel Prober and Intelligent Quant Path Selector
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce decode and prefill latency impact of mixed-precision and dequant steps by selecting kernels and scheduling microbatches based on low-overhead per-model/shape profiling.

Background: We see 6-12% p50 latency regressions on long-context decode when the runtime picks conservative FP32 paths for some attention blocks. There is also measurable token-level cost from repeated dequant/requant operations when headwise precision toggles across layers. Existing heuristics are static and coarse-grained (model architecture or user-specified). This ticket proposes an adaptive in-service prober that measures microbenchmarks for attention kernels and an online path selector that combines a dequant-cost score with latency/cost objectives to pick INT8/FP8 or mixed precision kernels per layer/sequence-length bucket.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Kernel prober collects per-model, per-seqlen microbenchmarks in <50ms overhead and writes results to runtime cache.
2) Path selector uses prober data + recent telemetry to choose kernel variants with measurable improvement: >=3% p50 latency reduction or >=6% token-cost reduction on at least two benchmark flows.
3) No regression >2% p99 across existing unit tests; rollout gated by canary traffic.
4) Integration tests covering fallbacks for unknown GPU type and for models with dynamic attention shapes.
5) PRs merged for runtime core, scheduler hook, and telemetry pipeline with dashboards linked.
design_notes:
High-level design: introduce a Kernel Prober component that runs nonblocking microbenchmarks the first time a model + seqlen pair is seen on a server. Prober returns a compact profile: latency per kernel variant (INT8-epilogue, FP8-optimized, mixed-precision), dequant CPU/GPU transfer cost estimate, and memory pressure signal.

Path selection policy: a lightweight scorer produces a single numeric 'dequant_score' and 'latency_delta' estimate per candidate kernel. The scheduler composes these with SLO weights to pick the kernel variant and also suggests microbatch ordering: prefer grouping tokens whose best kernel is the same to reduce churn.

Prefill/Decode scheduling changes: add a microbatch reordering pass in the prefill pipeline that prioritizes contiguous tokens by kernel affinity, plus an optional 'shadowed KV' mode where we maintain a parallel low-precision KV copy for hot prefixes to avoid repeated full dequant roundtrips.

Trade-offs considered: probing frequency vs cold-start overhead; we limit probes to at most one per model-seqlen per host and use probabilistic sampling on high-cardinality workloads. Shadowed KV uses extra VRAM; we only enable it when memory headroom > 15% and predicted token savings exceed estimated memory cost.
implementation_plan:
1) Prototype Kernel Prober as server-side async task (Maya) — gather microbenchmarks for tiny inputs (B=1, seqlen buckets 16/64/256) and persist into LRU profile cache.
2) Implement kernel score API in runtime core (Rafael) to expose candidate variants and quick estimated deltas.
3) Scheduler hook: microbatch affinity grouping and shadowed KV maintenance logic.
4) Telemetry: emit kernel_choice, probe_latency, dequant_estimate to metrics pipeline.
5) End-to-end canary: enable for runtime-1.22 on a small fleet with two models and run AB for two weeks, collect dashboards.
6) Rollout plan and rollback path documented in runtime runbook.
telemetry_and_metrics:
Emit the following metrics: kernel_prober.duration_ms, kernel_choice.count by variant, kernel_choice.latency_estimate, dequant_bytes_estimate, shadow_kv.memory_usage, microbatch_affinity.hit_ratio.

Dashboards: per-model kernel histogram, p50/p95/p99 latency by chosen kernel, token-cost delta estimates. Set alert if p99 increases by >2% post-rollout.

Bench harness: run on A100, H100, and T4-equivalent shapes; record per-seqlen improvements and memory impact. Attachments below contain initial run results.
